facts.statement: The genus Paraplesiobatis was described by Broili in 1933.
The only known species is Paraplesiobatis heinrichsi.
Paraplesiobatis lived in Early Devonian Germany.
facts.quote: from the Hunsrückschiefer Lagerstätte of Early Devonian Germany

facts.statement: Paraplesiobatis was a lightly armored placoderm belonging to the order Pseudopetalichthyida.
facts.quote: is a lightly armored pseudopetalichthyid placoderm

facts.statement: The single known specimen measures 10 centimeters in total length and includes a plate-covered head and part of the vertebral column.
facts.quote: consisting of a large, incomplete, plate-covered head, and some of the vertebral column, with a total length of 10 centimeters

facts.statement: Experts suggest that Paraplesiobatis may belong to the same genus or species as Pseudopetalichthys due to strong resemblance.
facts.quote: The specimen strongly resembles Pseudopetalichthys to the point that many experts suggest they may be of the same genus or species

facts.statement: It is debated whether Paraplesiobatis and Pseudopetalichthys are the same, but a decision cannot be made until better preserved specimens are discovered.
facts.quote: talk of synonymizing the two cannot begin (let alone continue) until more, better preserved specimens are found

facts.statement: Paraplesiobatis lived during the Emsian stage, between 410.62 and 399.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Emsian to Emsian (410.62 to 399.5 million years ago)
